message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Standard atomic weight** | ~1.008 u (average of isotopes) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ/mol) |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ/mol) |
| **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ/mol (negative → endothermic) |
| **Molecular form at STP** | Diatomic molecule (H₂) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.9 °C (20.44 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g/L (≈0.00008988 g/cm³) |
| **Specific heat capacity (gas)** | 28.836 J/(mol·K) |
| **Heat of formation (ΔHf°)** | 0 kJ/mol (by definition for elemental H₂) |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2H or D), Tritium (^3H or T) |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ/mol |
| **Typical uses** | Fuel cells, ammonia synthesis (Haber process), rocket propellant (liquid H₂ + liquid O₂), laboratory standard gas |

**Quick Facts**

* Lightest element; most abundant in the universe (~75 % of baryonic mass).
* Highly reactive; forms hydrides with many metals and nonmetals.
* Flammable with air (explosive range ≈4–75 % vol. in air).
* In its metallic phase under extreme pressure (>400 GPa) predicted to become superconductive at low temperatures.

These values give you a snapshot of hydrogen’s fundamental physical and chemical behavior.
